text.p: Greek construction firm Terna announced on Monday the acquisition of majority stakes in two smaller construction companies and plans to diversify into other business activities.
Terna's management told shareholders at the annual meeting it bought an 85 percent stake into Etka SA, a smaller construction company, holder of a 'Z-class' works certificate.
Terna also acquired a majority stake in a company specialising in metal construction and industrial engineering works -- Biomek SA.
The cost of these corporate moves was not disclosed.
Shareholders were also told that their company was diversifying into wind power projects through its Terna Energy subsidiary.
The latter will construct a 3.7 billion drachma wind power site carrying a 35 pate subsidy for the set up of a 10.2 MW power unit in the island of Evia.
The uncompleted portion of Terna's order book is valued in excess of 24 billion drachmas.
A dividend per share of 65 drachmas for fiscal 1996 was declared, versus 100 a year earlier.
The stock will trade ex-dividend June 24.
Terna's 1996 pretax earnings rose 6 percent to 1.603 billion drachmas on ver growth of 30 percent to 8.849 billion.
Its shares were quoted unchanged at 1,090 drachmas on Monday in thin volume of 5,960 shares. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
